conclusion: The MISEV2023 consensus (ev-misev2023-quality-framework) supports the reviewers' guideline-backed conclusions that orthogonal characterization, separation from non‑vesicular particles, transparent production reporting, and appropriate controls (orthogonal QC panel, validated intact‑EV assays, and stability‑indicating potency assays) are recommended prerequisites before advancing an EV intranasal formulation into cross‑species delivery testing. However, any program‑specific assertions that SGL‑001 has (or has not) produced an MCB/WCB, completed validated intact‑EV release assays (with LLOQ, specificity, precision), developed a stability‑indicating potency assay linked to in vivo PD, or demonstrated reproducible GMP‑like batch production are unsupported by the supplied evidence, because the supplied record contains only the MISEV guideline and no SGL‑001 CMC/assay/scale‑up documentation.
unsupported_assertions: That SGL‑001 has produced a characterized MCB/WCB (master/working cell bank) — no program MCB/WCB records were supplied in the provided evidence.
That SGL‑001 has validated intact‑EV release assays with documented LLOQ, specificity, and precision — no assay validation reports were supplied.
That SGL‑001 has a stability‑indicating potency assay that is linked to an in vivo PD measure — no stability or potency linkage reports were supplied.

That SGL‑001 has produced ≥3 GMP‑like manufacturing runs with release and batch comparability data demonstrating reproducible production — no batch manufacturing/run reports or comparability data were supplied.
That formulation/device compatibility has been demonstrated for intact‑EV recovery ex vivo or in vivo for SGL‑001 — no formulation/device compatibility study reports were supplied.
